title: Phayao on a Budget: 2 Days 1 Night Under 1,000 THB | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A real budget backpacker plan for Phayao, Thailand: 2 days 1 night with lakeside rooms at 250-400 THB, free temples around town, and khao soi for 40-60 THB a bowl. Doable for under 1,000 THB per person.
keywords: Phayao budget travel, Phayao backpacking, cheap Phayao accommodation, Phayao 2 day 1 night itinerary
h1:
Phayao on a Budget
Backpacking 2 Days 1 Night
intro: Phayao is one of the best-value towns in the north if you're watching your wallet. Walking the shore of Kwan Phayao lake is free, the pretty temples around town don't charge entry, khao soi runs 40-60 THB a bowl, and lakeside rooms start at just over 200 THB a night. We've laid out a 2-day, 1-night plan with the budget broken down to the baht, and you can do all of it without your own car.

blocks.html: A lot of people assume a trip up north means saving up a big lump sum, but Phayao is the exception where you can have a great time on a thin budget. The town is small enough to walk across, the food is cheap, lakeside rooms are friendly on the wallet, and most of the highlights — Kwan Phayao, Wat Sri Khom Kham, Wat Tilok Aram — barely cost anything to enter. We've set this plan at around 900-1,100 THB per person (not counting the fare to get to Phayao). Here's how it works.

blocks.text: The whole-trip budget, broken down to the baht

blocks.html: These are real numbers based on current room rates and restaurant prices in Phayao, figured per person. Travel as a pair and split the room and it drops even lower.

items: 1 night's stay — lakeside guesthouse/homestay from ฿250-400 (split between two people, that's ฿125-200 each)
4-5 meals — khao soi, khanom jeen nam ngiao, made-to-order dishes by the lake, ฿250-350 total
Getting around town — rent a motorbike for ฿250-300 a day, or cycle around the lake for free
Entry fees — most temples are free; the boat out to Wat Tilok Aram is ฿20-30

blocks.title: A money-saver that actually works
blocks.html: If there are two of you, book a single room with a double bed and split it — that pulls your accommodation cost down to a bit over a hundred baht each, leaving you cash for a few more good meals.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Phayao trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Phayao
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: The cheapest way to get to Phayao

blocks.html: Phayao has no airport, so most budget travelers take a coach from Bangkok. An air-conditioned coach (Sombat Tour or Greenbus, for example) runs about ฿650-1,025 each way depending on the class of bus, and the trip takes around 9-10 hours. Taking an overnight bus saves you a night's accommodation. The other option is to fly into Chiang Rai and continue by minivan or local bus into Phayao, about another 1.5 hours.

items: Bangkok-Phayao coach — from Mo Chit 2, around ฿650-1,025, a 9-10 hr ride
Fly to Chiang Rai + transfer — faster but the airfare costs more; worth it if you catch a cheap flight
Around Phayao — rent a motorbike for ฿250-300 a day; it's by far the easiest way up the hill to Wat Analayo

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: The lakeshore, the temple on the water, and a morning Buddha

items.activity: Start the morning with khao soi at Saeng Phian, Tha Kwan
items.note: A shop going back more than 40 years; chicken or beef khao soi at ฿40-60 a bowl, and they do khanom jeen nam ngiao too. Open 08:00-17:00.

items.activity: Stroll the shore of Kwan Phayao, the largest freshwater lake in the north
items.note: Walking is free, and there are spots to rent a bike and ride along the lake. The morning air is just right.

items.activity: Take the boat to Wat Tilok Aram, the temple in the middle of the lake, to pay respects to a 500-year-old stone Buddha
items.note: The return boat is about ฿20-30 per person — it's a photo spot locals in Phayao are proud of.

items.activity: Lunch at a made-to-order spot by the lake — order gaeng hang lay, larb, and tom yum fish
items.note: Places like Chid Lom Chom Kwan serve northern and Isan dishes at fair prices, with a free lake view thrown in.

items.activity: Pay respects to Phra Chao Ton Luang at Wat Sri Khom Kham by the lake
items.note: The largest Chiang Saen-style Buddha image in Lanna, free to enter; you can walk on to the cultural hall afterward.

items.activity: Find a lakeside cafe, catch the breeze, and wait for sunset
items.note: Coffee is ฿50-70 a cup, and the sunset behind the lake is gorgeous in the evening.

items.activity: Dinner at the market or a place in town, then walk back to your room
items.note: Save your energy for the hill tomorrow morning.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Up to Doi Analayo, grab some souvenirs, head home

items.activity: An easy breakfast near your room, then rent a motorbike
items.note: Wat Analayo sits on a hill about 20 km out of town — a motorbike is the most convenient way up.

items.activity: Head up to Wat Analayo Thipayaram (Doi Busarakham) for the Buddha images and the view over town
items.note: Free to enter. From up high you can see the whole of Kwan Phayao — go early when the sky is clearer.

items.activity: Come back down and visit any in-town temples you haven't seen yet
items.note: Several temples in town are within walking distance of each other, with no entry fee.

items.activity: Close the trip with a lunch of khanom jeen nam ngiao, or khao soi from a shop you haven't tried yet
items.note: Leave time to pick up local souvenirs like khaep mu (pork crackling), sai ua sausage, and chili dips.

items.activity: Return the bike, pack up, and get ready for the bus home
items.note: Take an evening coach and you'll roll into Bangkok the next morning.

blocks.html: Phayao eats well on a budget of mere tens of baht. Local dishes are easy to find and friendly on the wallet — here are the spots and dishes that give the best value if you're traveling light on cash.

items.name: Khao Soi Saeng Phian (Tha Kwan)
items.blurb: A khao soi shop going back more than 40 years near Tha Kwan; soft noodles, a rich curry broth, with chicken, beef, and khanom jeen / nam ngiao noodles all on the menu.

items.name: Khanom Jeen Nam Ngiao
items.blurb: A morning favorite up north — a well-rounded nam ngiao broth over rice noodles, eaten with pork crackling and fresh greens. A filling meal for tens of baht, found all over town.

items.name: Lakeside made-to-order (Chid Lom Chom Kwan)
items.blurb: A restaurant right on the lake with northern and Isan dishes — gaeng hang lay, duck larb, tom yum fish. Order to share among a group and it's even better value, with a lake view for free.

items.name: Khao Soi Him Khong (Dok Kham Tai)
items.blurb: Over on the Dok Kham Tai side, across from the municipal office; several styles of khao soi — chicken, beef, pork, meatball — plus other northern dishes. Worth a stop if you're passing through.

items.name: Local souvenirs
items.blurb: Khaep mu (pork crackling), sai ua sausage, chili dips, and pla som (fermented fish) from the lake — take them home as gifts for just a few tens of baht, found at the markets in town.

blocks.title: Eating well on a budget
blocks.html: Traveling in a group? Order 3-4 shared dishes in the middle of the table and add extra steamed rice — it's cheaper than everyone ordering their own single plate, and you get to try more dishes in one meal.

Part of Phayao's charm is that lakeside rooms are still not pricey. Plenty of guesthouses and homestays start at just over 200 THB a night, and some rooms have big windows looking out over the lake and the mountains.

items.name: In-town guesthouse / B&B
items.blurb: Small, clean rooms from ฿250-300 a night, within walking distance of the lake and the restaurants. Good for backpackers staying a single night.

items.name: Lakeside homestay
items.blurb: A relaxed, friendly feel; some include breakfast, and you wake up to the lake view. Still within budget.

items.name: Minimalist stay near the lake
items.blurb: Clean, simple rooms with double-bed and family options — split it among a few people and it gets even cheaper.

blocks.text: Free things to do in Phayao

items: Walk or cycle around Kwan Phayao — the largest freshwater lake in the north; strolling costs nothing
Pay respects to Phra Chao Ton Luang at Wat Sri Khom Kham — a giant Buddha by the lake, free to enter
Head up to Wat Analayo on Doi Busarakham — views of the town and lake from up high, no entry fee
Watch the sunset by the lake — a photo spot locals love, free every evening
Wander the in-town market — taste local food and see how people live, without paying a thing

faq.q: How much does 2 days 1 night in Phayao cost?
faq.a: Backpacking it — a lakeside room at 250-400 THB a night, local meals for tens of baht each, and most highlights free to enter — your budget in Phayao runs around 900-1,100 THB per person, not counting the fare from Bangkok. Travel as a pair and split the room and it's cheaper still.

faq.q: What's the cheapest way to get to Phayao?
faq.a: Take an air-conditioned coach from Mo Chit 2 for about 650-1,025 THB each way, a 9-10 hour ride. Pick an overnight bus and you save a night's accommodation. The other option is to fly into Chiang Rai and continue by road into Phayao, about another 1.5 hours — good if you can catch a cheap flight.

faq.q: How do you get around Phayao without a car?
faq.a: The town is small — you can walk to the lake, Wat Sri Khom Kham, and the restaurants. Around the lake there are bikes to rent for riding along the shore. To get up to Wat Analayo on the hill, about 20 km out of town, renting a motorbike for 250-300 THB a day is the more convenient bet.

faq.q: What are the cheap eats in Phayao?
faq.a: Khao soi is the staple, at 40-60 THB a bowl; Saeng Phian near Tha Kwan has been open for more than 40 years. Khanom jeen nam ngiao for breakfast runs about 35-50 THB and is found all over town. With a group, ordering shared dishes for the table and topping up with steamed rice works out cheaper than everyone getting a single plate.

faq.q: Does Phayao have free things to do?
faq.a: Almost everything is free — walking and cycling around Kwan Phayao, paying respects to Phra Chao Ton Luang at Wat Sri Khom Kham, heading up to Wat Analayo for the view over town, and watching the sunset by the lake all cost nothing. The only fee is the 20-30 THB boat out to Wat Tilok Aram in the middle of the lake.
